assumptions: Issue 2301 is repo-maintenance owned by a repository session, not the orchestrator; Step 3 landed as 1dcf196ea9b506ec14feb55e8465b53d9faf1706, which is this branch's base

Capacity and preview are separate truths. The old reconcileFlow collapsed both into a single status word, so one unreadable preview edge reported the whole run UNVERIFIABLE and hid every other lane's readable capacity answer

The top-level status keeps its exact previous meaning, so no consumer reading only that word is affected. The only NEW way to reach UNVERIFIABLE is capacity_error, a field that did not exist before, so no run a consumer has already seen can be reclassified
Action ordering (relinquish, then resume, then ready) is preserved so the existing consumer assertion in reconcile.test.mjs stays a true statement about the code rather than being rewritten to fit it

Expiry is not abandonment. An expired lease means a clock ran out; abandonment is a separate fact that exists only if somebody wrote the evidence down. Expiry alone never mutates and never suggests a mutation

queued_behind of null means UNKNOWN, never zero. 'Nothing is waiting behind this expired lane' is a reason not to act; 'the queue was unreadable' is not, and coercing one into the other would manufacture a reason
The queued-behind computation is lazy and memoized, so only a snapshot containing at least one expired lane pays for openWorkIssues() and buildDynamicQueues()

assertAbandonmentEvidence returns null for an ordinary blocker, so the marker requirement and the explicit worktree-state requirement cannot reach the existing ordinary relinquishment path or its tests

The flow adapter's relinquishCapacity passes no worktree state, so automatic reconciliation of an abandonment-audit blocker now refuses rather than completing. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour, not an accidental throw: no automated caller can observe somebody else's disk, and the plan requires that reconciliation never automatically transitions an expired claim. It is pinned by a test that asserts the refusal and then asserts the same evidence is accepted once an operator supplies the observation

RELINQUISH_WORKTREE_STATES duplicates WORKTREE_STATES across a module boundary rather than importing it, so a test asserts the two are equal; a drifted suggestion would tell an operator to run a command with a value that command refuses

Three new prose comments originally used the word 'missing', which the throughput truth audit discovers as call sites; the first push failed with 'truth-audit semantic inventory drift (found 299, recorded 296)'. Two ways to satisfy that check exist: record three excluded dispositions in the audit inventory, or say the same thing in words the audit does not claim. Recording them would have put this pull request on docs/verification/throughput-guard-truth-audit-20260828.json, which open pull requests 2823 and 2821 already hold, and the single-ready-PR collision rule is a rule to wait behind, not to bypass. The comments were therefore reworded to 'absent', 'unreadable' and 'omits'. Their meaning is unchanged and none of them ever described a database object that was never created, so the truth audit loses nothing: it still records 296 call sites and its own suite still passes.
